## Parking

Cars, vans and trucks park on the grounds at Gate 9 located at 875 Memorial Avenue (Public Parking) . Several adjacent private parking lots are located in the neighborhoods along Memorial Avenue and are not affiliated with Eastern States Exposition. Cash only is accepted in our auto parking gates. There are no ATMs near Gate 9.

---

Bicycles and scooters can park for free at 915 Memorial Avenue.

Our paved handicapped parking area is located inside the Gate 9 parking area at Gate 9A. The number of accessible spaces we offer far exceeds the code requirement, accommodating 580 vehicles, on a first-come, first-served basis. We also isolate a two-acre plot in the immediate vicinity of the gate where we can park up to 1,000 cars of handicapped patrons. Since we attempt to accommodate every handicapped vehicle, that area is vast and not totally paved. The Gate 9A area also includes a covered drop-off area that may be used to drop-off/pick up handicapped, elderly or otherwise impaired passengers to wait while their car is parked.

Motor coaches and buses park off-site with continuous round trip shuttle service to and from fairgrounds for drivers. There is free parking with advance registration.

# General Info

## Join Us at The Big E!

#### Sept. 18-Oct. 4, 2026

The Big E is the largest event on the East Coast and the fourth largest fair in North America. Attendees can enjoy hours of free entertainment and attractions, terrific food, plus the best that New England—and beyond—has to offer. Highlights include authentic New Orleans Mardi Gras in The Big Parade, an immersive Ireland adventure in the International Plaza’s Dingle Peninsula Showcase, North American Midway, as well as countless educational opportunities from the Avenue of States to Storrowton Village Museum, Farm-A-Rama and more. The Big E offers a diverse and vibrant experience to visitors from throughout the country.

_

## Fairtime Hours

Gates: 8amThe Big E Bakery: 9am–10:30pm

Buildings and Craft Common: 10am–10pm

Avenue of States: 10am–9pmStorrowton Village Museum & Shops: 10am–9pmNew England Center: 10am–9pmMidway: Sunday–Thursday, 11am–10pm; Friday–Saturday, 10am–11pm_

## FAQ

The Big E is an annual event that begins on the second Friday after Labor Day and runs for 17 days. Eastern States Exposition is home to the Fair. ESE is not owned by any specific individual or group and is organized as a not-for-profit, educational institution under the laws of the Commonwealth of Massachusetts. Its governing body is a volunteer Board of Trustees consisting of distinguished civic, business and agricultural leaders from each of the six New England states.

---

Gates: 8amThe Big E Bakery: 9am - 10:30pmBuildings and Craft Common: 10am - 10pmAvenue of States and Storrowton Village Museum & Shops: 10am - 9pmNew England Center: 10am - 9pmMidway: Sunday-Thursday, 11am - 10pm; Friday-Saturday, 10am - 11pm

---

No weapons are allowed on the grounds. Metal detectors are in use at every entrance gate to the fairgrounds and bags are subject to search at gates. Our Security staff is comprised of Big E Security personnel as well as dedicated members of the West Springfield Police Force. The Security office is located on Hampden Avenue and is open the Monday before Opening Day and throughout the Fair, 24-hours a day. The full services of the West Springfield Fire Department are available on our grounds 24-hours a day during the Fair at the Fire Station on Hampden Avenue. The First Aid Station and the Lost People Center (LPC) is located across from the Fire Station, staffed daily by dedicated, caring professionals. Guests are encouraged to seek assistance from the LPC immediately upon discovering when someone has been separated from their group. The LPC also maintains a waiting area and outside message board for postings. ALL lost and found items should be brought to the LPC.

---

All guest entering through the gates are subject to search. Weapons detection devices are being utilized at each gate. To ensure guest have a safe and enjoyable time at The Big E, the following items are not permitted at The Big E.• Weapons, including knives over 1.5” of any kind. • Mace or Pepper spray• Drones• Alcohol• Contraband• Illegal drugs and controlled substance, drug paraphernalia including ANY form of marijuana• Explosives• Ammunition• Sticks, bats, poles, sling shots• Fireworks, Sparklers• Toys that replicate actual guns• Spears, machete, blades• Laser pointers• Noise makers• Balloons• Handcuffs or flex cuffs• Stun guns• Cans or glass bottles, aerosol cans (exception spray sunscreens)• Skateboards• Bicycles• In-line skates• Hover boards• Lawn chairs, stadium seats• Kites, inflatables or balloons• Rubber band guns or any device designed to launch or propel any type of projectile. • Pets except authorized Service animals- (See Service Animals Policy)• Other carry-ins as determined by The Big E management.

---

Yes. Guests may bring unopened, sealed plastic water bottles onto the fairgrounds. You may also bring an empty, refillable water bottle. Please note that glass bottles of any kind are not permitted.

---

Experience something new every day of the Fair by aligning your schedule with The Big E’s themed days. Walk through one of the State Buildings and visit its exhibits or watch The Big Parade, which honors each day in a special way. Live locally? Be sure to come on the day honoring your city or town and run into friends, neighbors and family! Click here to view this year's listing of Special & State Days.

---

We recommend coming to The Big E on weekdays if you are looking for a more relaxed experience. If weather is good on weekends, you can expect large crowds and traffic delays.

---

On-site parking for cars/trucks is available for $10 (cash only) at Gate 9. Motorcycles can park for $5 (cash only) at Gate 9. Bicycles can park for free at 915 Memorial Avenue. The Big E provides 1,200 handicapped accessible parking spaces at Gate 9 on a first-come, first-served basis. The Gate 9A area is available for drop-off/pick-up of passengers and has a large canvas tent with benches for patrons.

---

We have 1,200 ADA parking spots located in Gate 9 with shuttle service. The parking is available on a first-come, first-served basis.

---

Wheelchairs and a limited number of oversized wheelchairs are $30 per day. Electric scooters are $80 per day and may not be available on extremely wet days. Wheelchairs and scooters from Scootaround can rented on the grounds during the Fair at Gates 4, 9A and at the Transportation Center. Strollers ($15), double strollers and wagons ($20) can also be rented at Gates 4 and 9A. If you would like to rent a scooter or wheelchair in advance you will need to make a reservation 24 hours prior to the day you plan to attend the Fair. Rent a scooter or wheelchair online. All reservations made in advance require a credit card payment to reserve over the phone or online. Walk up rentals have the option to pay with cash or credit.

---

Parking spaces at Gate 9 are available on a first come, first served basis for visitors with self-contained and pop-up campers. Spaces per day are $40 and additional cars are $10 per space/per day. Visitors with tents are $20 per space/per day cars are $10 per space/per day. Portable restroom facilities are nearby though no other amenities will be provided during Fairtime.

---

Service animals, including service animals in training, are allowed through the gates. Fairgoers are not allowed to bring pets or emotional support animals. Learn why we only allow service animals on our grounds.

---

ATM's can be found along the Avenue of States and inside the Coliseum, Young Building, Better Living Center, Mallary Complex, Food Court, Transportation Center and the Midway. Machines are also located near the Flag Plaza, Lost & Found/First Aid, Craft Common, Info booth near Gate 2, as well as Gates 1, 4, 5 and 7.

---

The Big E Gates and Midway accept Apple Pay, Google Pay and Tap to Pay (contactless) payments. Many vendors accept these payment types as well, although it's best to ask before ordering.

---

The Nursing Mothers Center is located inside the First Aid Building, located on Hampden Avenue.

---

Lost an item? Please call our Lost & Found at (413) 205-5164 and the staff will be able to assist you.

---

Eastern States Exposition does not permit professional photography equipment on the fairgrounds during The Big E. This policy is in place to ensure a safe and enjoyable experience for all attendees.

---

Eastern States Exposition does not permit the use of drones on the Fairgrounds during The Big E. This policy is enforced by the Massachusetts State Police Drone Team to ensure the safety and security of all attendees.

---

The Big E is a family-friendly event. All guests are required to wear shirts, pants and shoes while on the grounds. Clothing that contains profane, obscene or otherwise offensive language or imagery is not permitted. Guests may be asked to cover, change or remove inappropriate attire in order to continue enjoying the fair.

---

For the safety of all guests, costumes are not permitted on the Fairgrounds. Only performers contracted by Eastern States Exposition may appear in costume or interact with guests in an entertainment capacity. This policy helps prevent confusion, protects the integrity of our entertainment program and ensures all performers are properly vetted and trained. Thank you for your understanding.

---

Yes. Eastern States Exposition (ESE), the nonprofit organization that operates The Big E, is a private entity. While we welcome millions of guests each year, admission to our fairgrounds is at our discretion. ESE reserves the right to remove or deny entry to any individual at any time, for any reason, to ensure the safety, comfort and enjoyment of all fairgoers.

---

Yes, but advance approval is required. All media representatives covering The Big E professionally must submit a media credential request to the Eastern States Exposition Marketing Department for review and approval prior to attending. Working members of the media who have not received proper approval and credentials are not permitted to be on the grounds in a professional capacity and may be removed if they attempt to conduct business without authorization.

---

Yes. Guests are welcome to share their personal experiences at The Big E on social media. Casual posting for personal accounts does not require approval.

---

Influencers who plan to produce content in a professional capacity—such as sponsored posts, brand collaborations or commercial promotions—must request approval from the Eastern States Exposition Marketing Department in advance. The Big E is a private, family-friendly event with strict brand, safety and conduct policies. Professional content creators, including influencers, must follow the same standards as working media. Approval ensures content creation is consistent with our mission and that all parties operate respectfully on the fairgrounds.

WEST SPRINGFIELD, Mass. (WWLP) – The Big E, the largest event on the East Coast and the fourth largest fair in North America, kicks off on Friday for a 17-day run.

The fair opens with Military Appreciation Day, offering free admission to active duty, retired military personnel, and veterans with a valid ID. Last year, the fair set a new attendance record with over 1.63 million visitors, and the second weekend was particularly busy, with Saturday seeing nearly 180,000 attendees.

Visitors are advised to avoid traveling to the fair between 8:30 a.m. and 11 a.m. to avoid traffic congestion, and late-night departures are also busy.

## When do the buildings and Midway open?

- Big E gates open at 8:00 a.m.
- The Big E Bakery is open from 9:00 a.m. to 10:30 p.m.
- Buildings and Craft Common is open from 10:00 a.m. to 10:00 p.m.
- The Avenue of States and Storrowton Village Museum & Shops are open from 10:00 a.m. to 9:00 p.m.
- The New England Center is open from 10:00 a.m. to 9:00 p.m.
- Midway is open Sunday through Thursday from 11:00 a.m. to 10:00 p.m. and Friday through Saturday at 10:00 a.m. to 11:00 p.m.

## When is my state/town day at The Big E?

Each day at the Big E honors something specific. For example, the first Friday is Military Appreciation Day at the Big E. Veterans, active duty military and their dependents all get in free. Here are all the special and state days this year:

- Friday, September 12 – Military Appreciation Day

## Admission Prices

The 2025 regular-price admission tickets are $20 for adults, $16 for seniors, and $12 for children ages 6 through 12, kids under 5 are free.

Presale tickets do offer a discount; however, all ticket sales are final. If you buy tickets in advance through September 10th, they are $17.50 for adults and $12 for children ages 6 through 12. If you plan to go to The Big E multiple times, there is a value pass option that gets you in daily during the 17 days of the fair for $71.50 per adult and $36.50 for children ages 6 through 12.

For $33.50, you can also get one wristband that includes unlimited rides at the Midway on the day you visit, Monday through Friday, or 78 credits on Saturday or Sunday.

## How much does parking cost?

If you plan to park on the Big E fairgrounds, all main parking will be found at Gate 9, which is the first gate on Memorial Avenue if you are coming from the east (from Springfield, Route 5, I-91, etc.) and the last gate if coming from the west (Agawam). It is cash-only parking, and there are no ATMs near the gate, so you will have to have $10 on hand to park. Motorcycles can park for $5 at Gate 9.

The 17-day long fair features hours of free entertainment and attractions, terrific food, authentic New Orleans Mardi Gras in The Big Parade, an immersive Ireland adventure in the International Plaza’s Dingle Peninsula Showcase, North American Midway, as well as educational opportunities from the Avenue of States to Storrowton Village Museum, Farm-A-Rama, and more.

# Accessibility Guide

_

## Personal Mobility Device Policy

The Big E is committed to providing an accessible and inclusive experience for all guests. To support individuals with mobility challenges, guests are permitted to bring personal mobility devices designed for use by individuals with disabilities.

Permitted devices on the grounds include:

- Manual and electric/power wheelchairs
- Personal mobility scooters (three- or four-wheeled, electric-powered)
- Other mobility aids that are designed specifically for and used by individuals with mobility-related disabilities

Please note:

- Only mobility devices intended for and used by individuals with limited mobility or mobility-related disabilities are allowed.
- Two- or one-wheeled electric or battery-operated scooters, hoverboards, skateboards, bicycles and other recreational or transportation devices that are not primarily designed for mobility assistance are not permitted on the grounds.
- All personal mobility devices must be operated safely and at walking speed.
- Guests using personal mobility devices may be asked by gate personnel whether the device is necessary due to a mobility disability, as permitted by the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA). Documentation is not required.
- All personal mobility devices are subject to search at the gates.

For guests who do not have a personal device, a limited number of mobility scooters and wheelchairs are available to rent on a first-come, first-served basis inside Gate 1B (Transportation Center), 4 and 9A entrances. You can make online reservations starting in August 2026.

We appreciate your cooperation in helping maintain a safe, accessible environment for all.

_

## Service Animals

Service animals, including those in training, are welcome on the Eastern States Exposition grounds. For the safety and comfort of all guests, pets and emotional support animals are not permitted.

Service animals are specifically trained to perform tasks that assist individuals with physical, intellectual or emotional disabilities. These animals are working partners—not pets—and may help their handlers navigate large crowds, respond to loud or unexpected noises, or assist during emergencies.

Under the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA), service animals are granted legal protections that do not extend to emotional support animals. Because emotional support animals and pets are not trained to perform specific tasks, they are not covered under the ADA. Allowing non-service animals on the fairgrounds could pose safety and liability risks; for example, if an unauthorized animal were to bite another guest, its owner would be held responsible, as could ESE.

To ensure a safe and welcoming experience for everyone, Eastern States Exposition permits only service animals on the fairgrounds.

_

## ADA-Accessible Restrooms

Eastern States Exposition provides ADA-accessible restrooms throughout the fairgrounds to ensure convenience and comfort for all guests. Accessible restroom stalls are available in the following locations:

- Better Living Center
- C Barn
- Coliseum
- Farm-A-Rama
- First Aid Station
- Food Court
- Hampden Avenue Restrooms
- Mallary Complex
- New England Center
- Transportation Center
- Visitors’ Center East
- Visitors' Center West
- West Road Restrooms
- Young Building / International Plaza

All restroom facilities meet or exceed ADA design standards. Restrooms are clearly marked with accessibility signage. View the fairgrounds map for a look at all locations.

_

## ADA-Accessible Vehicle Parking at Gate 9

Located at 875 Memorial Avenue, West Springfield, Mass., Gate 9 is the public parking lot for The Big E. The fairgrounds provide a dedicated handicapped/accessible parking area within the Gate 9 lot, specifically at Gate 9A.

The Big E offers more than 1,200 ADA-accessible parking spaces at Gate 9. Accessible parking is available on a first-come, first-served basis and guests who require these spaces are encouraged to arrive early, as demand is high during peak attendance days.

The parking fee is $10 (cash only) for cars and trucks.

Complimentary shuttles operate within Gate 9A, transporting guests from their vehicles to the entrance gate for convenient access to the fairgrounds.

_

## Entertainment Venue Accessibility

In accordance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA), only manual and power wheelchairs are permitted within designated ADA seating areas at The Big E’s entertainment venues. Due to space limitations and safety concerns, other power-driven mobility devices (OPDMDs)—including electric scooters—are not permitted inside the Big Top, the premium seating section of the Court of Honor Stage, or The Big E Arena.Guests are solely responsible for their devices. Any OPDMD left unattended in these areas may be relocated by security or operations personnel to ensure a safe environment for all attendees.Each venue includes marked ADA-accessible seating that meets or exceeds ADA capacity and design standards, providing a safe and inclusive experience for guests using manual or power wheelchairs.Please note that Eastern States Exposition does not require guests to remain seated during performances at The Big E Arena or Court of Honor Stage. The Big TopOPDMDs must be parked in the designated scooter and stroller/wagon parking area inside the marquee tent. These devices are not permitted beyond the seating perimeter. Manual and power wheelchairs may be parked in designated wheelchair ringside boxes (1 and 21).Guests with mobility challenges who do not use a wheelchair may sit in the first row of bleacher seats at walkway level, marked with the ADA logo. All seats and wheelchair locations are available on a first-come, first-served basis. Please ask an usher for assistance.Please note that there are no public restrooms located inside The Big Top. The closest ADA-accessible restrooms are located across Springfield Road in the Better Living Center. The Big E ArenaThe Big E Arena features a wheelchair platform at floor level for individuals using manual or power wheelchairs, plus companion seats. In select floor seating sections, chairs marked with an ADA logo on the seating map can be removed to accommodate wheelchairs.OPDMDs are not permitted inside the Arena or parked within the immediate boundaries of the Court of Honor Stage seating area. There are no designated parking areas for OPDMDs outside the Arena perimeter.Please note that The Big E Arena is a no re-entry venue. ADA-accessible portable restrooms are available within the Arena’s restroom section for guests with accessibility needs.All ADA-designated seats are available for purchase online and are sold on a first-come, first-served basis. If the seating map shows that ADA areas are sold out, they are sold out. No ADA seats will be released on the day of the show, and ushers will not be able to accommodate ADA seating requests at that time. If you require a wheelchair-accessible seat and have purchased a ticket in a non-ADA section, please contact the Box Office in advance for assistance. Court of Honor StageThe Court of Honor Stage is a free, open-seating venue featuring bench seating in the immediate viewing area and a park-like lawn surrounding the stage. This venue does not include a wheelchair platform._

# The Big E 2025: What to know as New England’s largest fair kicks off Friday

By Nathaniel Rosenberg, Staff WriterSep 9, 2025

Share to Facebook Share to Twitter Share to bluesky Share from Email

Spectators walk through an area of The Big E in West Springfield, Mass., in a file photo.

Keith Whamond

The biggest fair on the East Coast returns this weekend, for 17 days packed with musical performances, agricultural showcases, and dozens of popular food vendors.

The Eastern States Exposition — better known as The Big E— returns to Massachusetts this Friday. The West Springfield-based fair, which drew more than 1.6 million people last year, is selling discounted tickets until Sept. 11, and features " Connecticut Day" on Sept. 17. With showcases from all six New England states, the event serves as an unmatched sampler of regional arts, crafts and cuisine.

One iconic Connecticut brand, Frank Pepe Pizzeria Napoletana, is making its debut at the festival and will be serving pizza in the Connecticut Building on Sept. 16, 17 and 18.

## When is The Big E 2025?

The Big E runs 17 days, from Friday, Sept. 12 to Sunday, Sept. 28. Gates open every day at 8 a.m., and most parts of the fair are open until 9 or 10 p.m. The Big E Bakery stays open until 10:30 p.m., and on Fridays and Saturdays, Midway, the amusement park portion of the festival, stays open until 11 p.m.

## Where is The Big E 2025?

The Big E 2025 will be held in West Springfield, Massachusetts, at its usual fairgrounds. Parking for the event, which costs $10 and is cash only, is located at 875 Memorial Ave. in West Springfield.

## How can I get tickets for The Big E 2025?

Tickets for The Big E 2025 are on sale now at the fair's website. Prices have largely held steady from the 2024 exhibition, though the advance tickets and 17-day passes both are slightly more expensive.

Advance tickets are available through Sept. 10 at 11:59 p.m. at a discounted rate of $17.50 for adults and $11.50 for children (ages 6-12). On Sept. 11, prices increase to $20 for adults and $12 for kids. Children under 5 get in for free.

Opening day this year is also Military Appreciation Day, when free admission is available to active duty military personnel and their dependents, as well as retired military and veterans (but not their dependents).

Danny Bell, the late owner of Little Taste of Texas in South Windsor and Smokehouse Grill at the Big E's Connecticut Building, visits with Gov. Ned Lamont at the fair in 2021.

Season passes for all 17 days also are available at $71.50 for adults and $36.50 for children.

Senior tickets (age 60 and over) are $16 between Sunday and Thursday. Additionally, anyone entering after 5 p.m. on those days can get a ticket for $11 at the gate.

## Who is performing at The Big E 2025?

This year features musical acts across three different stages — The Big E Arena, which is for headlining acts and requires extra tickets, the Court of Honor Stage, which has free shows with admission to the fair, and The E Stage, which features up-and-coming artists.

Some notable performers this year include Busta Rhymes and Rick Ross, The Avett Brothers, Foreigner, TLC and Big Boi, Train, ZZ Top, The Kid Laroi, B.o.B, Queensrÿche and The Marshall Tucker Band.

Article continues below this ad

## What new food is there at The Big E 2025?

The Big E is known for offering outrageous foods, and this year is no exception. Offerings include a barbecue sundae, pickled doughnuts and deep-fried Oreos. This year, new foods include a deep-fried strawberry shortcake, both a pickle sundae and a pickle shake, and an apple pie-flavored cider.

The new and improved Big E Craz-E Burger, also available in a spicy version, is built on two doughnuts: one glazed and one plain, each serving as a bun

Leeanne Griffin / Hearst Connecticut Media

New Connecticut vendors at the fair include Manchester's The Hop Knot– which offers "pretzel-wrapped creations" – BrightSide Brew Kombucha, which is sold throughout the state, and Veegmyeats, a Hartford-based vegan bakery.

## What activities are there at The Big E 2025?

For younger children, there is the Circus Spectacular, a giant slide and petting zoo. Teens and young adults may gravitate toward the " North American Midway," which boasts a number of classic fair games. The Big Parade kicks off nightly at 6 p.m.

There will be livestock competitions as well, featuring pigs, sheep, goats, cattle and sheepdogs.

Guests also can stop by the recently renovated Connecticut Building on the Avenue of States, which is modeled after the original statehouse building. Inside are businesses, vendors and foods highlighting the best in Connecticut culture, including a beer garden and a "pizza throne" fashioned by New Haven artist Michael Pollack. The UConn Women's Basketball National Championship trophy also will be on display at the fair.

The Avenue of States also hosts buildings for the other five New England states, and the fair includes a number of craft vendors dotting the grounds.

The Big E (Eastern States Exposition) 2026 MA: Complete Guide - Global Shop

Every September, a small city rises along Memorial Avenue in West Springfield, Massachusetts. For 17 days, it fills with the smell of cream puffs, the sound of parade bands, and the energy of more than a million visitors from across New England and beyond. It is the Eastern States Exposition, known to everyone simply as the Big E. It is the largest fair on the East Coast and one of the top ten fairs in all of North America.

Thank you for reading this post, don't forget to subscribe!

This guide covers everything you need to plan your visit, from dates and ticket prices to the best food, top attractions, and insider tips for making the most of your time at the fairgrounds.

Table of Contents

Toggle

## Dates, Location and Key Event Details

| Detail | Information |
| --- | --- |
| Event Name | The Big E (Eastern States Exposition) |
| Dates | September 18 through October 4, 2026 |
| Duration | 17 consecutive days |
| Venue | Eastern States Exposition, 1305 Memorial Avenue |
| Location | West Springfield, Massachusetts 01089 |
| Phone | 413-737-2443 |
| Website | thebige.com |
| Admission | Adults $20, Children ages 6 to 12 $15, Children under 6 free |
| Parking | $10 for cars and trucks at Gate 9 (cash only), $5 for motorcycles |
| Bicycle Parking | Free at 915 Memorial Avenue |

The fair has run continuously since 1916. This year’s edition marks 110 years of the Eastern States Exposition tradition. The fairgrounds open at 8:00 a.m. daily. The Big E Bakery opens at 9:00 a.m. All other buildings, the Avenue of States, Storrowton Village Museum, the New England Center, and the Craft Common open at 10:00 a.m. Rides open at 10:00 a.m. on Fridays and Saturdays and at 11:00 a.m. Sunday through Thursday.

## Daily Schedule at a Glance

| Area | Opening Time | Closing Time |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Fair Gates | 8:00 a.m. | Varies |
| Big E Bakery | 9:00 a.m. | Varies |
| Buildings and Craft Common | 10:00 a.m. | 10:00 p.m. |
| Avenue of States and Storrowton | 10:00 a.m. | 9:00 p.m. |
| New England Center | 10:00 a.m. | 9:00 p.m. |
| Midway Rides (Sun–Thu) | 11:00 a.m. | 10:00 p.m. |

A daily parade rolls through the fairgrounds each morning starting at 10:00 a.m. It features marching bands, floats, draft horses, livestock, and performers. Arriving before 10:00 a.m. gives you the best spot along the parade route and lets you get ahead of the midday crowds.

## The Avenue of States: The Heart of the Fair

The Avenue of States is what makes this fair unlike any other in America. Six dedicated buildings line the avenue, one for each of the New England states: Maine, New Hampshire, Vermont, Massachusetts, Connecticut, and Rhode Island. Each building showcases the food, crafts, agricultural products, local businesses, and culture unique to that state.

Walking the Avenue feels like taking a road trip through New England in a single afternoon. You can taste Maine seafood chowder, pick up Vermont maple syrup, sample Connecticut craft products, and discover Rhode Island specialties, all without leaving the fairgrounds. For many visitors, this is the single most rewarding part of the entire experience.

Massachusetts Day falls on September 24, 2026, and Harvest New England Day takes place on October 2, 2026. Both are special programming days within the Massachusetts Building that feature games, giveaways, and entertainment highlighting the culture, agriculture, and tourism of the state.

## Top Attractions at the 2026 Fair

### Storrowton Village Museum

Storrowton Village Museum is one of the most historically significant attractions on the fairgrounds. It features a reconstructed 18th and 19th-century New England village assembled around a traditional town green. Nine authentic buildings were moved from Massachusetts and New Hampshire to create this living history exhibit. Visitors can take guided tours, explore the historic structures, and engage in hands-on educational programs about early New England life. The Sam Adams Beer Garden operates within the Storrowton grounds, offering craft beer, live acoustic music, and food in a relaxed outdoor setting.

### The Big E Super Circus

The Big E Super Circus runs every day of the fair. It is a full-scale, multi-act circus featuring performers that appeal to all ages. The circus is free with fair admission and runs multiple shows throughout each day. It consistently ranks as one of the most popular draws on the fairgrounds, drawing large crowds from opening through closing.

### The Giant Slide

The Giant Slide has been at the fair since 1969. It stands 46 feet tall and runs 135 feet long, making it one of the iconic landmarks on the fairgrounds. Ride tickets are purchased at the slide itself. Generations of New Englanders have ridden it, and it remains a genuine fair tradition for families.

### Grandstand Concerts

The Big E books headline musical acts throughout its 17-day run. Confirmed acts for 2026 include Ice Cube on October 3 at 7:30 p.m. and Jet on September 28. Fair admission is included with concert tickets, but grandstand seating requires a separate concert ticket. These shows sell out, therefore booking your concert ticket early through the official website is essential.

### Competitive Exhibits and Livestock Shows

The fair has deep agricultural roots, and the competitive exhibits reflect that. Livestock shows feature cattle, sheep, goats, horses, and poultry judged across dozens of categories. Produce competitions, baking contests, quilting displays, and craft exhibits fill the exhibition halls. These competitions showcase the genuine agricultural heritage of New England and give visitors a window into the farming communities that have supported the fair for over a century.

### The Better Living Center and Young Building

For those who enjoy shopping, the Better Living Center and the Young Building are home to hundreds of vendors selling crafts, home goods, decor, kitchen products, and seasonal items at fair-exclusive prices. Many visitors use these buildings to get a head start on holiday gift shopping. The vendor variety is extensive, and the deals are often not available anywhere else.

## Food: The Real Reason People Come Back

The fair’s food scene is legendary across New England. The Big E Cream Puff is the undisputed star. These giant choux pastry shells are filled with fresh whipped cream and baked fresh on the grounds. The line is always long and it is always worth it. The bakery opens at 9:00 a.m., and arriving early is the best way to beat the wait.

Beyond the cream puff, the food options span the full range of fair cuisine and international flavors. Classic options include clam chowder, lobster rolls, BBQ pork, sausage and peppers, corn dogs, and loaded baked potatoes. International vendors serve Mexican, Chinese, Greek, Latin, German, Polish, Italian, and Indian food. Additionally, newer fair food creations rotate each year. Past editions have featured a doughnut smash burger and a sloppy joe sandwich inside fried dough.

Beverage options include craft beers at the Harpoon Beer Hall, specialty martinis at the Ketel One Martini Bar, rum and sangria buckets, and boots of beer at The Wurst Haus. Gluten-free and vegan options are also available from dedicated vendors on the fairgrounds.

## Tickets, Discounts and Special Days

Adult admission at the gate is $20. Children ages 6 to 12 pay $15. Children under 6 always enter free. Tickets purchased online in advance may offer savings over gate pricing. Checking the official website before your visit is worthwhile.

Special discount days are offered throughout the fair. Military appreciation is honored on designated days, with free admission available for active duty military personnel, dependents, retired military, and veterans who present valid identification at the gate. Additional discounted admission days and group rates are available, so reviewing the official schedule at thebige.com before you visit will help you plan around the best value.

## Practical Visitor Tips

- Arrive early. Gates open at 8:00 a.m., which gives you time to enjoy the bakery and settle in before the parade starts at 10:00 a.m.
- Visit on a weekday. Tuesday and Wednesday offer dramatically smaller crowds compared to weekends. Lines are shorter, parking is easier, and the experience is more relaxed.
- Wear comfortable shoes. The fairgrounds are large and you will spend hours on your feet across different zones and buildings.
- Bring cash. Parking at Gate 9 accepts cash only. Many smaller food vendors also prefer cash.
- Book concert tickets separately and in advance. Grandstand shows sell out early.
- Check the daily schedule online before you go. Programming varies by day, and you do not want to miss special events that only happen once or twice during the fair.
- Service animals are welcome. Pets are not permitted on the fairgrounds.
- Bags are allowed but are subject to security checks at the entrance.

## Getting There

The Eastern States Exposition sits at 1305 Memorial Avenue in West Springfield, Massachusetts. The fairgrounds are accessible by car from Interstate 91. On-site parking at Gate 9 costs $10 for cars and trucks (cash only) and $5 for motorcycles. Free bicycle parking is available at 915 Memorial Avenue. During peak weekend days, traffic on Memorial Avenue can back up significantly. Arriving before 9:30 a.m. on weekends is the most reliable way to find parking and get settled before the crowds build.

Shuttle services from nearby locations are also available during the fair. Checking local transit options and park-and-ride programs on the official website before your visit can save time and frustration on busy days.

## Conclusion

The Big E 2026 runs from September 18 through October 4 at the Eastern States Exposition in West Springfield, Massachusetts, delivering 17 straight days of New England tradition, food, music, agriculture, and entertainment. Adult admission is $20 at the gate, with free entry for children under 6 and discounts available on special days. The Avenue of States, Storrowton Village Museum, the Super Circus, the Giant Slide, and grandstand concerts by Ice Cube and Jet headline the attraction list. The Big E Cream Puff, the daily parade, the livestock shows, and the hundreds of food vendors and shopping exhibitors round out an experience that draws over 1.7 million visitors annually. Whether you come for the cream puffs, the concerts, the history, or the chance to sample all of New England in a single afternoon, there is no fair in the region that matches what West Springfield puts together every September.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### When and where is the Big E 2026?

The Eastern States Exposition 2026 runs from Friday, September 18, through Sunday, October 4, 2026, at 1305 Memorial Avenue, West Springfield, Massachusetts. The fair runs for 17 consecutive days. Gates open at 8:00 a.m. daily.

### How much does it cost to attend?

Adult admission at the gate costs $20. Children ages 6 to 12 pay $15. Children under 6 enter free. Parking for cars and trucks is $10 at Gate 9 and must be paid in cash. Grandstand concert tickets are sold separately and are not included with general fair admission.

### What is the best day to visit to avoid crowds?

Weekdays, particularly Tuesday and Wednesday, are significantly less crowded than weekends. If your schedule allows, a mid-week visit offers shorter lines, easier parking, and a more relaxed experience overall. Weekends tend to be busier but offer more grandstand entertainment and higher energy.

### What are the must-try foods at the fair?

The Big E Cream Puff is the signature item and should be the first stop for any visitor. The bakery opens at 9:00 a.m., and arriving early avoids the longest lines. Other must-tries include clam chowder, lobster rolls, BBQ pork, and the rotating selection of creative new fair foods that are introduced each year.

### Are concerts included with fair admission?

General fair admission does not include grandstand concert seats. Concert tickets must be purchased separately through thebige.com. However, standard admission includes the Big E Super Circus, the daily parade, and all other entertainment on the fairgrounds. Headline acts like Ice Cube and Jet often sell out quickly, so book your concert tickets early.

# Big E Parking and Getting There: How to Avoid the Stress

April 7, 2026J Tarbox4 min read

---

The Big E draws over a million visitors across its 17-day run. That's a lot of cars, a lot of traffic, and a lot of people who didn't plan ahead and are now sitting in gridlock on Route 147 wondering why they didn't leave earlier.

Getting to the Big E doesn't have to be stressful — but it does require a plan. Here's how to handle the logistics so you can spend your energy on cream puffs instead of parking anxiety.

## Driving to the Big E

The Eastern States Exposition grounds are in West Springfield, Massachusetts, just off I-91 near the Connecticut border. It's within a two-hour drive of most of New England, which is part of why it draws such enormous crowds.

From Boston: About 90 minutes west on the Mass Pike (I-90) to I-91 South.

From Hartford: About 30 minutes north on I-91.

From Burlington, VT: About 3 hours south via I-89 and I-91.

From Portland, ME: About 3 hours southwest via the Maine Turnpike and I-90.

The approaches to the fairgrounds get congested during peak hours, especially on weekends. The worst traffic is typically between 10 a.m. and 1 p.m. on Saturdays and Sundays.

## Parking

The Big E has large parking areas, but they fill up — especially on weekends and during the opening and closing weekends of the fair. A few things to know:

Parking is paid. There's a flat fee per vehicle (check the Big E website for current pricing). Cash speeds things up at the lots, though many now accept cards.

Arrive before 10 a.m. on weekends. The closest lots fill first. If you arrive after noon on a Saturday, expect a long walk from your car to the gates.

Note where you parked. Take a photo of your lot number or a nearby landmark. After eight hours of walking the fair, everything looks different, and wandering a parking lot at 9 p.m. is nobody's idea of fun.

Plan for the walk. Even in the closer lots, you're looking at a 5–10 minute walk to the gates. In the farther lots, it can be 15–20 minutes. Wear comfortable shoes for the whole day, not just the fairgrounds.

## Shuttle and Transit Options

Many regional transit authorities and community organizations run shuttle services to the Big E during its 17-day run. These are often the easiest and least stressful way to get there, especially on peak days.

Check with your local transit authority — PVTA (Pioneer Valley Transit Authority) runs expanded service during the Big E, and other regional providers often offer bus routes from surrounding towns.

School and community group shuttles are sometimes available from towns across western Massachusetts, Connecticut, and beyond. Check local event listings.

Rideshare (Uber/Lyft) works well for drop-off and pickup, though surge pricing can be significant on weekend evenings. The drop-off area is usually near the main gate.

## When to Go (From a Logistics Perspective)

Weekdays are dramatically easier. Tuesday through Thursday during the Big E's run is a completely different experience from a weekend. Less traffic, easier parking, shorter lines inside, and a more relaxed atmosphere overall. If you can take a day off work, it's worth it.

Opening weekend draws huge crowds — everyone's excited for the first days. Closing weekend also draws big numbers as people rush to get in before it ends. The middle weekends are the sweet spot if you must go on a Saturday or Sunday.

Evening visits can work well if you don't mind skipping the morning programming. Traffic into the fair tends to ease after 4 p.m. as earlier visitors leave, and the midway and Avenue of States are well-lit and lively into the evening. Just know that some livestock and agricultural events are morning-only.

## What to Bring

Cash. For parking, food vendors, and game booths. ATMs on the grounds have long lines and fees.

Comfortable walking shoes. You'll cover a lot of ground — the Big E fairgrounds are large, and between the Avenue of States, the midway, the livestock barns, and the walk from parking, you can easily log five miles or more.

A light jacket or layers. September weather in western Massachusetts can be unpredictable — warm afternoons and cool evenings are typical.

A phone charger. You'll use your phone for photos, schedules, mobile tickets, and navigation. A portable battery keeps you from going dark at 6 p.m.
